accepts.because: a build request to find patterns for. The briefing comes back on `brief`; the original question rides along in it

a nudge to reconcile the catalogue against the colony's own template registry. The corpus is a seed, so it describes the library of the moment this librarian was born; anything registered since -- an `add_templates`, a hand-dropped directory plus a rescan -- is resolvable at the mutation door and invisible here until this lane is driven (GH #496). The body is not read: the message IS the nudge

a params-only update for one cell of this hive or of a sealed hive in it (GH #1353): `hop.subscriber` is the cell's absolute path, the body carries `params` and nothing else. The inner edges carry it to that cell by the end of the path; a cell of another path applies nothing. Answered by exactly one `params_applied` or `params_refused`. Draw it only from the operator's road

emits.because: the request plus the patterns found for it, for the authoring cell behind this librarian. Retrieval is an enhancement: a failed lookup comes back here too, degraded and marked, and never hangs a build

the reconciliation's own report -- how many templates the registry holds, how many the corpus already carried, how many rows were written, and which names. Counted on the hop (`catalogue_known`, `catalogue_ingested`) so a run that found nothing is distinguishable from one that did not run. A refusal comes back here too, named and with the corpus untouched
the cell named by `hop.subscriber` of an `in_params` update merged it into its live params (GH #1353)
the cell named by `hop.subscriber` of an `in_params` update refused it whole: `hop.refused_subscriber` is its path, `hop.error_code` the code and the body the detail (GH #1353)
